edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Comm. Cant. Liber I 13

source_text: Introduxit me rex in cellaria sua. Cellaria sunt secreta sapientiae, thesauri scientiae absconditi. Rex Christus introducit animam de foris ad interiora, de littera ad spiritum, de historia ad mysterium. Exsultabimus et laetabimur in te: laetitia non in cellariis ipsis, sed in rege qui introducit.
pass_a_gloss: He-brought-in me king into chambers his. Chambers are secrets of-wisdom, treasuries of-knowledge hidden. King Christ brings-in soul from outside unto interiors...
pass_b_english: [[The king has brought me into his chambers >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:4]]. The chambers are the secrets of wisdom, hidden treasuries of knowledge. King Christ brings the soul from outside to what is within, from letter to spirit, from history to mystery. We will exult and rejoice in you: joy not in the chambers themselves, but in the king who brings her in.
